purpose: Locate repeated work in verified memory opening before selecting the next implementation patch.
scope: Input admission claim ownership fix plus read-only performance diagnosis of memory; no new storage format or read optimization in this stage.

revision.working_tree: Uncommitted accumulated PR108 patches; exact product sources are pinned below. No commit or push.

method.instrumentation: Separate cProfile intervals activated through Python 3.12 sys.monitoring for actual ordinary open/court/replay; explicit API intervals for independent reads. Product methods are not replaced.
method.nested_intervals: An active outer interval owns nested calls; replay performed inside court is included there, not profiled again as an independent interval.
method.self_accounting: Categories partition all observed function self time. other_self remains explicit and includes unclassified builtins. Inclusive function times overlap and must not be summed.
method.file_accounting: Read-open audit events, posix.read calls and unique file sizes after the run are separate metrics. None measures physical disk bytes or cache misses.
method.reader_modes: Fresh and reused describe Python reader objects, not OS cache; no cache clearing. Held guard profiles exclude guard-entry scan, reported separately.
method.source_stability: All product Python hashes and all original corpus file hashes matched before/after capture and again when this report was generated.
method.harness_hashes: Final harness hashes captured after analysis. measure.py and scopes.py remained unchanged during capture; profile_report.py classification was refined after capture.

corpus.scenario: Original storage evacuation: 24 nodes, 6 racks, 1536 shards, 3 replicas; node12 fails after 24 moves, node5 capacity is corrected to 8, stale action is refused before replanning. Profile workloads investigate the retained incident on copies.
corpus.materialized_snapshot: Windows4/5 contain no MEMORY_STATE. Three additional real durable investigations create window8 with one MEMORY_STATE. Preparation is outside read profiles; no hand-fabricated snapshot.
preserved_checks: Full state equality on fresh/reused/held-guard reads at each dataset window.
Configuration identity and boundary maps preserved across repeated readers.
Historical saved run reopens its recorded boundary.
Uninstrumented/profiled audit full search event SHA256 identical.
Frozen lexical reference equality plus 3150 independently checked candidates per audit.
Canonical court and replay succeed; zero transport effects in both audits and snapshot preparation.
corpus.different_histories: Window4, window5 and window8 have different histories. Their elapsed times are not an A/B estimate of snapshot benefit.

uninstrumented_control.scope: Timed durable execution includes consolidation; authentic corpus creation, cloning, reference comparisons, state inspection and replay are separate.

profiled_audit.scope: Timed durable execution includes consolidation; authentic corpus creation, cloning, reference comparisons, state inspection and replay are separate.

inputs.accounting: Audit events count read-only file opens, not bytes read or disk I/O. Sizes describe unique files after the run; repeated opens do not multiply unique bytes.

findings: Ordinary open scans once; examB fresh/reused scans four times each; externally reopened replay pin scans twice. The earlier approximately 5.6s owner+session figure described examB, not every ordinary session opening.
A reused reader skips decoding unchanged records but still physically checks and copies them. Window4 configuration reads 17 events and makes 833790 recursive deepcopy calls.
Ordinary court scans three times, calls _read 57 times and deepcopy 10551499 times including recursion. This is not a count of distinct objects or allocated bytes.
Window8 held-guard state uses the actual materialized snapshot: zero apply_report calls, yet 2075201 recursive deepcopy calls. Snapshot presence alone does not remove copying the inventory.

Fresh decode redundantly validates/canonicalizes the same decoded data: strict decoder proves exact canonical bytes, after which store _read canonicalizes again. Warm decoded-reader cache already bypasses this work.

next_patch_proposal.first: Remove only the repeated canonical(event) != raw comparison from ProjectMemoryStore._read after strict decode has established it. Not implemented here.
next_patch_proposal.proof: decode_canonical and canonical use identical profile/codec identifiers. The decoder canonicalizes the private decoded JSON tree and compares exact bytes before returning it. No user code mutates it between decode and the redundant comparison.
retain: Physical committed-transaction validation and hashing on every read.
Record size/schema/kind/job_key/payload checks, marker identity and receipt checks.
Detached caller results and existing cache lifetime.
All court, authority, replay and storage-format contracts.
acceptance: Malformed/noncanonical event bytes with a valid physical commit marker must still be rejected by the decoder, with existing typed errors.
Exact canonical positive cases, old records, mutation isolation and repeated reads remain unchanged.
Paired uninstrumented ordinary/exam/replay/consolidation measurements on the same authentic heavy corpus; include first and reused reader separately.
next_patch_proposal.later: Global decoder redundant validation is a broader codec change; guard-scoped reuse needs its own ownership/lifetime/publication-invalidations contract. Shared storage/snapshots, compact frame and native kernel remain separate stages.

limits: One uninstrumented audit is a scale control, not a paired speedup measurement or a median.
All 34 profile intervals are instrumented diagnostics; do not extrapolate their timings to uninstrumented wall-time shares.
This stage does not measure RSS, peak RAM, cold disk reads or a Rust/C#/SQLite replacement.
API historical pin reopen is not full CLI resume.
No Gold REQUESTED/FRAME_COMPLETED or worker-frame reference-resolution profiling is claimed.
Claim custody acceptance is separately recorded in reports/memory_admission_input_custody_v1.json.
